## Bio

I am a physics PhD student at the **University of Massachusetts Amherst**, working with Prof. Benjamin Heidenreich at the Amherst Center for Fundamental Interactions. My research develops theoretical and computational tools to understand strongly coupled quantum field theories, drawing on string theory, conformal field theory, and numerical methods.

My path to physics was shaped by a fascination with the mathematical structures underlying nature — from the geometry of extra dimensions to the entanglement patterns of quantum matter.

## Research Interests

- **String Theory & High-Energy Physics**
  - Lagrangian descriptions of non-Lagrangian $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFTs via geometric engineering
  - $\mathcal{N}=1$ flavor orientifolds: discrete torsion, Wilson lines, and S-duality
  - Quad-CFTs and infrared phases of theories with tensor matter
  - Mirror geometry in type IIA with D6/O6-branes
  - 2D CFT discrete gaugings and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

- **Condensed Matter & Many-Body Physics**
  - Symmetry-enriched criticality and boundary RG flows in Majorana chains
  - Monte Carlo algorithms for long-range Coulomb interactions
  - Superfluidity and phase transitions in 3D Bose gases

- **Computational Methods**
  - Tensor networks (DMRG, MPS) for extracting conformal data
  - Worm-algorithm Monte Carlo for path-integral simulations

- **Future Directions**
  - Generalized symmetries (higher-form, non-invertible, categorical) as a bridge between string-theoretic SCFTs and lattice models of quantum matter

For a detailed overview, see the [Research](research.qmd) page or browse the [Notes & Expositions](notes/index.qmd).
